task_text: Create two buffered zones from the input features and compute the area where the two buffer zones overlap.
Compute the logarithm of the input raster, summarize it over the zones, build a mask from the input raster, and count the valid pixels per zone of the summarized zones.
Sample the raster values at the input point locations and add a new attribute to the sampled points.
Clip the event features to the region boundary and split any multipart geometries of the clipped features into single parts.
Merge the downloaded layers into one layer and keep only the relevant attribute fields.
Clip the input layer to the study boundary and dissolve the clipped features.
Derive the coordinate attributes of the line features -- the starting and ending point coordinates of each line -- as a chain of computed fields.

Locate suitable areas for new schools: clip the population data to the boundary, keep the high-population areas, buffer the existing schools and the rivers, combine the buffer zones, remove them from the high-population areas, and clip the result back to the boundary.
Reproject the area-of-interest layer and rasterize it onto the raster grid.
Merge the input layers and compute the regions where the input layer overlaps the merged features.
Clip the raster to the target extent and reproject the clipped raster to the target coordinate reference system.

Assess vegetation degradation: derive the degradation and improvement significance masks from the change raster and the significance raster, align both to the target grid, and compute the hotspot mask from the aligned rasters.

Assess flood exposure of buildings: buffer the hazard zones, derive the representative point of each building, select the points inside the hazard buffers, and sample the raster values at those points.
Convert the cost-distance raster to polygons, join the administrative attributes to the settlement points, then join the point attributes to the resulting polygons.
Bring the plot layer into the raster's coordinate reference system and compute zonal statistics of the raster over the reprojected plots.

Assess flood exposure: derive the flood extent from a raster, convert it to polygons, buffer the waterways, combine the flood polygons and the buffered waterways into a single flood-impact layer, and extract the exposed areas from it.
Reproject the line layer, buffer the reprojected lines, erase the buffered region from the target layer, and split any multipart features of the remaining areas into single parts.
Reproject the stream segments and, from the reprojected segments, extract two separate outputs: the starting vertices of every segment and the ending vertices of every segment.
Build a series of nested buffer zones around the road network, then combine them through successive unions into a single overall impact-area layer.
Reproject the input layer to the target coordinate reference system.
